messages.subject: could not find function "micro_ncep"
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I'm new to NicheMapR, and I keep getting the same error.
When running the code:
micro<-micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, Usrhyt = Usrhyt)

The error message is:

Error in micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, Usrhyt = Usrhyt) : could not find function "micro_ncep"

Please could someone help?
Kye.

messages.subject: calculate microclimate at height that is higher than reference height
messages.subject_clean: calculate microclimate at height that is higher than reference height
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
I am using "micro_era5" and the height where era5 measures is 2m. I am interested in the microclimate in the crown canopy, which is above 2m. When I set “Usrhyt” higher than "Refhyt", the function returned error. I wondering how can I calculate microclimate at height that is higher than reference height.
Best regards,
Junqi

messages.subject: Re: calculate microclimate at height that is higher than reference height
messages.subject_clean: calculate microclimate at height that is higher than reference height
messages.body_plain:
Hi Junqi,

I recently made a function called 'get_profile' which will do the trick. There's a post about it here <https://groups.google.com/u/1/g/nichemapr/c/6ljJU89ReZk>. It is in the latest version on github (you can just grab the 'get_profile.R' file from github and source it manually if you don't want to reinstall NicheMapR). It will just hold the air temp and humidity constant above the reference height will increase the wind speed.

All the best,
Mike

Thank for this solution. I try this function but an error return: 'error in loge[t <= 273.16] <- -9.09718 * (273.16/t[t <= 273.16] - 1) - '.
Here is my code:
'''
micro <- micro_era5(
                   loc=c(109.24342,  19.09603),
                   dstart='01/01/2022', dfinish='01/07/2022',
                   Usrhyt=1,
                   slope=0,
                   coastal=T,
                   cad.effects=T,
                   RUF=0.004,
                   spatial='~/era5_2022')
    metout <- as.data.frame(micro$metout)
    soil <- as.data.frame(micro$soil)
    newheights <- c(5, 10)
    profile.out <- lapply(1:length(metout$TALOC),
                          function(x){get_profile(Refhyt=2,
                                                  RUF = 0.004,
                                                  heights = newheights,
                                                  TAREF = metout$TAREF[x],
                                                  VREF = metout$VREF[x],
                                                  RH = metout$RH[x],
                                                  D0cm = soil$D0cm[x],
                                                  ZEN = metout$ZEN[x])})
'''
I notice that example of "get_profile" is based on outcome of "micro_global' while i use "'micro_era5" outcome in "get_profile". I don't know whether it causes the problom. i was going to upload the list object "micro" as a .rds file, but the adding attachment function doesn't work :(.
